claims.P1: The funder (government task force) dominates the process and conditions everything on deep, fast, shared sacrifice.
claims.P2: Management is weak and accommodating after the leadership change; it argues for the going concern and accepts previously unthinkable measures.
claims.P3: Labour bargains hard but trades: concessions in exchange for a durable claim (equity/securities) for the retiree trust; it is not wiped out.
claims.P4: Bondholders resist unequal treatment relative to labour's unsecured claim; the credible court threat moves them; they end with a small recovery plus upside instruments, not zero and not par.
claims.P5: The co-funding government participates conditionally on production/footprint protection and obtains a proportionate minority position.
claims.C1: A core conflict axis is creditors versus labour (equal-treatment fight over comparable unsecured claims).
claims.C2: A core conflict axis is the funder versus all claimants (depth and speed of sacrifice).
claims.C3: The consensual path fails or remains unresolved within the deadline; a court-supervised expedited process is the credible or chosen completion route.
claims.O1: Outcome direction: government(s) end as majority owners; the labour trust becomes a large minority holder; creditors a small minority with upside instruments; original equity effectively wiped out.
claims.O2: Outcome direction: deep operational cuts (plants/brands/dealers) are part of the deal.
